title: Gavin Newsom signs laws to protect California workers from AI threat
content:
Democratic governor sharply critical of Donald Trump for not passing comprehensive federal AI regulations

Governor Gavin Newsom signed laws Wednesday aimed at protecting California workers from the threats of artificial intelligence , including potential job losses and workplace surveillance.

The laws ban employers from using the technology to predict a worker’s emotional state by using their biometric data, require employers to send written notices to workers if AI is responsible for mass layoffs and ban employers from relying on AI to decide to fire someone.

title: Someone ‘Torturing’ LLMs in a Robot Prison Has Triggered the Dumbest Debate in AI Yet
content: One of the most heated discussions occurring on X at the moment is about the ethics of a GitHub project in which a person is running Saw-like “torture” and “pain” experiments on a series of locally hosted large language models, causing a series of effective altruists and people who believe LLMs are sentient to beg GitHub to delete the project on the grounds that the AI is suffering and that this glorified text adventure game is somehow cruel. The saga is an outgrowth of several recent viral papers and blog posts that have sparked a wildly tiresome conversation about AI consciousness and the idea of “model welfare,” which is essentially worrying about the “mental health” of AI bots and agents.

title: A new publication examines the cumulative impacts of the green transition on traditional Sámi livelihoods
content:
30.09.2026

  • Share on FaceBook
  • Share on LinkedIn

    • Researcher | Arctic Centre, the University of Lapland

    In Nordic cooperation made report “Towards understanding and managing cumulative impacts in Sápmi: approaches & collaboration – Workshop Report with focus on spatial data, reindeer and reindeer herding” explores the use of spatial data and methods in assessing cumulative impacts on traditional Sámi livelihoods.

    The impacts of the green transition on Sápmi and reindeer herding areas have been increasing due to factors such as forestry, rare-earth mineral mining, and the production of hydroelectric and wind power. The planning processes for these past, ongoing, and future projects are highly fragmented; consequently, the cumulative impacts of the projects and the perspectives of local people have not been adequately considered during the planning stages. Assessing the impacts of both historical and new activities in Sápmi requires concepts, frameworks, and tools capable of addressing cumulative impacts across space, time, sectors, and borders, as well as a stronger knowledge base to support just decision-making.

title: Analysis: Wind and solar save UK from gas imports worth £5.9bn during Hormuz crisis
content:
The UK has avoided the need for gas imports worth £5.9bn since the start of the Hormuz crisis as a result of record generation from wind and solar, reveals Carbon Brief analysis.

While gas prices are surging to levels not seen since the 2022 energy crisis, the UK has been generating record amounts of power from wind and solar, up 14% year-on-year.

This unprecedented clean-power generation is directly cutting the need for gas-fired electricity, which is down by nearly 10% year-on-year in 2026 to date.

In total, wind and solar have generated a record 41% share of the UK’s electricity needs in 2026 to date, compared with 25% from gas, according to Carbon Brief’s analysis.

The figure below shows that wind and solar has avoided the need for UK gas imports worth £5.9bn, since the outbreak of war between the US and Iran in February 2026.

These avoided gas imports would have required the UK to secure the equivalent of more than 100 additional tanker deliveries of liquefied natural gas (LNG).

The £1.3bn import saving in September 2026 to date is the result of record wind and solar output, at nearly 10 terawatt hours (TWh), combined with surging gas prices.

title: Russia’s Rage Fixes on the British
content:
British statecraft has “lived free in Russia’s head” for hundreds of years, in the words of a former UK defense attaché in Moscow. The historian Mark Galeotti noted that, over the last century, “Perfidious Albion” was, in Russia’s eyes, its “most cunning and devious foe”.

From this soil, fed by £25 bn ($33 bn) of UK aid to Ukraine since 2022, has emerged an eruption of suspicion and hostility. It may yet produce something more menacing than the current torrent of Kremlin-inspired verbal barrages.

Russia is run in part by a siloviki of former Soviet security officials who were spoon-fed distrust of the British as part of their training. It is part of their lore that London did terrible harm to the Bolsheviks and then the Soviet era, and that British intelligence chalked up significant triumphs at their expense. In this worldview, British attempts to undermine Russian power and greatness are part of an old game.

The flip side is the strange magnetism of Britain for the Russian elite; there have been massive Russian investments in British real estate, academia, and legal and financial sectors which have led to the sobriquet ‘Londongrad’ for the second home of many oligarchs.

title: Youth perspectives on polarisation: When does difference become division?
content:
From Finland to Armenia and Palestine, young people encounter polarisation in different forms. Yet across these contexts, similar questions emerge about trust, belonging, participation and the spaces available for dialogue. These themes were at the heart of CMI’s webinar that brought together young voices to reflect on how divisions shape their societies and what role young people can play in addressing them.

The webinar, organised as part of the annual Youth Peace Week Finland’s programme, explored how polarisation affects young people in everyday life and how they navigate increasingly divided social and political environments. The discussion featured youth worker and peacebuilder Liana Vahanyan from Armenia, communications professional and researcher Atta Khaled from Palestine, and Finnish youth activist Heta Uhtio. The conversation was moderated by CMI’s Project Officer Shekeba Ahmadi and can be watched through a recording.

title: Openness & Digital Sovereignty: Who Sustains the Commons?
content:
We are in a critical moment for the open web, and must raise the issues of openness and the commons to the level of public dialogue as we try to steer AI development to serve the public interest. We are also in a moment when open is being hailed as a panacea for digital sovereignty. This warrants interrogation.

On September 21st, Creative Commons convened leading experts, practitioners, and builders for a day of conversation about the collaborative underpinnings of openness, investigating all the layers of the stack for a better, shared understanding of what openness can—and cannot—do to help communities and nations drive towards digital sovereignty.

This event was made possible through the generous support of the Siegel Family Endowment. We are grateful to our co-hosts at the NYU Engelberg Center for making the space for a conversation like this.

Clear throughlines from the convening were:

  • Openness creates choices
  • Sovereignty depends on our ability to exercise and sustain those choices
  • Sustaining the people, institutions, and shared resources that make openness possible must be part of any sensible sovereignty strategy

title: 80 Years After Nuremberg Trials, U.S. Leads Assault on ICC & International Law: Wolfgang Kaleck
content:
Eight decades after the Nuremberg trials against Nazi war criminals, the Trump administration has launched an all-out assault on the International Criminal Court, primarily over the tribunal’s pursuit of Israeli leaders for war crimes committed in Gaza. In his recent address to the United Nations, President Donald Trump called the ICC a “rogue institution” and urged other states to abandon it, and his administration has vowed to dismantle it through sanctions and other pressure tactics.

“It’s so sad to remember that the core group behind the Nuremberg trials were Robert Jackson, Telford Taylor and Benjamin Ferencz, the U.S. prosecutors,” says Wolfgang Kaleck, lawyer and founder of the European Center for Constitutional and Human Rights. His new book is The Power of Law: Reconciling Legality and International Justice.

title: Preserving Indigenous Stories and Voices: WikiKathā Documented Nine Endangered Indigenous Languages in Indonesia
content:
Amid rapid modernization and development that frequently displace indigenous communities, many regional languages in Indonesia find themselves increasingly marginalized. Responding to the threat facing this oral heritage, Wikimedia Indonesia (WMID), in collaboration with the Alliance of Indigenous Peoples of the Archipelago (AMAN), through the Wikimedia Foundation Knowledge Equity Fund launched a collaborative project titled WikiKathā.

The name WikiKathā is derived from combining the word wiki and the Sanskrit word कथा (kathā), meaning ‘story’—which was subsequently absorbed as ‘kata’ (word) in the Malay language. Through this project, contributors aim not only to digitally preserve vocabulary, but also to safeguard the stories and cultural values embedded behind them.

Unlike general regional language documentation projects, WikiKathā focuses specifically on indigenous languages that receive little attention, are threatened with extinction, and are difficult to access. From August 2025 to May 2026, teams of fieldworkers and indigenous youth traveled to various remote corners of the archipelago.

title: 72 Hours or Two Weeks? Europe Takes Different Approaches to How Prepared People Should Be for a Crisis
content:
This raises the same practical question across Europe: how long should an individual household be able to cope on its own?

Some countries already have a clear answer – at least 72 hours. Others recommend being prepared for three to seven days, or even two weeks in certain scenarios. In some countries, there is no general preparedness timeframe at all.

The differences are not limited to the number of days. Countries also have different ideas about what preparedness actually means: in some, it means having water, food and medicines at home; elsewhere, it also includes alternative heating, cooking, electricity and communication, as well as access to civil protection infrastructure.

Three days have become something of a symbol of civil preparedness in Europe in recent years.

title: Victory! California Appeals Court Refuses to Revive Surveillance Tech CEO’s Meritless Lawsuit Against Journalist
content:
When the rich and powerful try to use the court to silence negative reporting about themselves, it’s worth calling out that behavior for what it is: an attack on free speech. This is why EFF is happy to stand up for reporters who find themselves in that situation.

The California Court of Appeals upheld a lower court’s decision to strike a former Premise Data CEO’s meritless lawsuit against a journalist who exposed the CEO’s secret arrest for felony domestic violence. Jack Poulson, the writer and publisher of All Source Intelligence, reported details from the San Francisco Police Department’s report of the arrest and posted a copy of the report after receiving the document from a confidential source. Poulson later learned the arrest record had been sealed. The CEO, Maury Blackman, sued Poulson, Substack, AWS, and another organization for damages to try and force the removal of Poulson’s reporting from the internet.

title: Mureneeko oikeusvaltio? Jukka Kekkonen luentovieraana Lahden pääkirjastossa 7.10.
content:
Ajankohtainen luentovierailu tutkii demokratian nykytilaa.


Meneillään oleva vuosituhat on muuttanut dramaattisesti maailman demokratioiden tilannetta. Yhteiskunnallisista puheenvuoroistaan tunnetuksi tulleen oikeushistorian ja roomalaisen oikeuden emeritusprofessori Jukka Kekkosen teos Mureneeko oikeusvaltio? kuvaa oikeusvaltiota ja siihen erottamattomasti liittyviä, perusoikeuksia uhkaavia kehityskulkuja kaikkialla maailmassa – myös Suomessa. Teoksesta on julkaistu toinen laitos tänä vuonna, ja siinä seurataan oikeusvaltiokehityksessä jatkuvasti tapahtuvia muutoksia tähän hetkeen asti.

Suomen ja Euroopan oikeushistorian tuntijana Kekkonen on erityisesti analysoinut demokratian tilan vaikutuksia erilaisten oikeuksien toteutumiseen.

Luento pidetään Lahden pääkirjaston auditoriossa keskiviikkona 7.10. klo 18.00. Luentovierailulla Kekkonen avaa teoksensa painavia ja ajankohtaisia teemoja.

Tilaisuus on kaikille avoin ja maksuton, sekä yleisökysymyksille on varattu aikaa.

title: Hub publishes policy paper and launches campaign to put cultural heritage at the heart of Public AI in Europe
content:
The EU-funded European Heritage Hub has published its policy paper “Beyond adopter and supplier: putting cultural heritage at the heart of Europe’s Public AI ecosystem”, released on 29 September on the occasion of the Hub’s Policy Talk  “INNOVATE. PROTECT. EMPOWER: How cultural heritage can make Public AI a reality” and is launching its dedicated advocacy campaign. Developed with the Europeana Foundation and with input from Hub partners across Europe, the paper highlights the role of the cultural heritage sector in the European Commission’s forthcoming AI strategy for the Cultural and Creative Sectors, expected in 2027. The campaign turns its key messages into a call for action: organisations and networks across Europe are invited to endorse it.

Read the policy paper · Read the executive summary

The AI strategy for the Cultural and Creative Sectors was announced in the Culture Compass for Europe published in November 2025. The Hub’s paper builds on “The case for Public AI: making it happen with cultural heritage”, published in June 2026, and on the responses that the Hub and the Europeana Foundation submitted to the Commission’s Call for evidence.

title: Denmark focuses on building favourable preconditions for Action Plan implementation
content:
On 28 September, Denmark hosted the first official meeting of the EU Strategy for the Baltic Sea Region National Coordinators Group. This meeting, followed by a full working day with a wider stakeholder group, marked the kick-off of the Danish Presidency 2026-2027.

Denmark’s Presidency of the EU Strategy for the Baltic Sea Region focuses on:

  • Ensuring an effective start to the implementation phase of the updated Action Plan (2026, pending European Commission approval). The Presidency encourages Policy Areas to use the first implementation phase to prepare the ground for their Actions to be taken forward across the Baltic Sea Region, including by identifying relevant partners, funding opportunities, and cooperation links with programmes, organisations, and actors in the region.
  • Increased Ukrainian involvement in the Strategy where relevant.
    The Presidency encourages Policy Areas and Steering Groups to take Ukraine into account when planning their work and to consider relevant opportunities for involving Ukrainian actors in Actions and cooperation activities.

title: Living better while living longer
content:
Europeans are living longer. This is one of the achievements of our social model. The question is whether we are living those additional years in good physical and mental health and whether this progress is shared equally across society.

The pursuit of longevity cannot simply mean adding years to life. It just as well means adding life to those years. In other words, extending the time in which we can take a full part in society, keep our relationships, feel accomplished and live with dignity. Importantly, though, healthy longevity must not become another privilege that correlates with income or social status. The right to healthy longevity needs to become an imperative of the progressive agenda for Europe.

title: How do you know when AI is wrong? Lessons from our AI x Investigative Journalism Forum
content:
Your story's data came from a scraper a reporter vibe-coded. The spot checks came back clean. Do you publish?

We opened the AI x Investigative Journalism Forum at The New York Times on Sept. 25 with that question, and 81% of attendees said they'd hold the story until someone reviewed the code. On the live polling app I built for the kickoff, attendees dragged a dot toward their answer, and 70% of the "hold" voters pushed theirs nearly all the way to the edge.

It was a snap judgment, made on phones in seconds. Reading the code is part of checking such a tool, but it won't tell you how often the output is wrong. For that, several speakers argued, you have to test the results.

That afternoon, Avery Schmitz of CNN taught attendees to vibe-code their own flight-tracking analysis and closed the workshop with his own stricter rule: "Never vibe code to a finding," and a checklist to go with it: check every finding against the raw source, reproduce the key claim and read the lines of code that produce it.

title: Tigray’s Renewed Conflict: How Drone Warfare is Reshaping the Battlefield
content:
By Daniel Tesfa, Shim Masha and Filmon Gebremikael

Addis Ababa | Ethiopia | 30 September 2026 (IDN) — Drone warfare reshapes Ethiopia–Tigray’s battlefield, while civilians relive the devastation of past wars.

From Pretoria to Renewed War

The Pretoria Agreement of November 2022, formally known as the Cessation of Hostilities Agreement (CoHA), was intended to end Ethiopia’s devastating Tigray war. Yet implementation faltered almost immediately. Internally displaced persons (IDPs) never returned to Western Tigray, which remained under the control of Amhara Fano militias, ENDF‑affiliated Tekeze Zeb units, and Eritrean forces. Large swathes of Eastern, Central, and Northwestern Tigray continued to be occupied by the Eritrean Army, undermining the credibility of the peace deal.

title: How to sustain journalism that rarely pays for itself
content:
Investigative journalism is expensive to produce and rarely pays for itself. A single story can require months of reporting, cross-border collaboration, specialist expertise and legal support, with no guarantee that the revenue it generates will cover those costs. For newsrooms doing this work, financial sustainability means finding ways to sustain reporting whose public value far exceeds its commercial return.

That makes decisions about revenue especially consequential. Time spent developing a new income stream is time a small team cannot spend investigating. Yet dependence on a narrow funding base can leave a newsroom vulnerable to shifting donor priorities or pressure from advertisers. The challenge is to identify sources of income that fit an organisation’s editorial mission, make sensible use of its limited resources and protect its independence.

title: Metrons & Logons: Morgane Billuart in Conversation with Matthew Johnstone
content:
Metrons and Logons brings together Matthew’s recent series of photographic works with display structures made by eva duerden. The images move between recognisable objects and architecturally processed surfaces, reminding us of objects we used to consider technical, while acknowledging their obsolescence. The longer one looks, the less clear that designation of time becomes. The result is a set of images that seem familiar but increasingly difficult to place, inviting the viewer to stare at pictures with an intrigued, yet suspicious eye. In this conversation, Matthew Johnstone and Morgane Billuart discuss what happens to an image when it unknowingly appears to be a testimony of a world that breaks down, and yet, perhaps, with another life force, an odd gaze, is starting anew.

Matthew Johnstone,  Repose_8176, 2025. Archival C-type print, PVC, Metrons & Logons, Turning Space, Berlin, 2026. Courtesy of the artist and Turning Space

Morgane

Matthew, in the show Metrons and Logons, what am I seeing exactly?

Matthew

title: Poison Pills
content:
Copyright reform is again on the horizon in Europe. Not only is the 2019 Directive on Copyright in the Digital Single Market under evaluation, but the European Commission has also called for evidence about a series of potential reforms and, just yesterday, 29 September, launched a targeted consultation.

One idea on the table is a possible reform of the Union’s copyright exception for research, to facilitate researchers’ work when engaging with copyrighted materials. There will be plenty of discussion about the precise wording of this in the months and years to come.

In this context, we will see the contours of a broader question: what are the aspects of copyright law that need to be avoided if we want to uphold the interests of users, the institutions they rely on, and society more broadly?

These legislative ‘poison pills’ sharply reduce the scope and beneficial impact of otherwise potentially beneficial legislative provisions. When engaging in copyright reform discussions, it is therefore valuable to look out for these and highlight the threat they pose early on.

Kaksikymmentäkaksi Suomen taide- ja kulttuurialan asiantuntijaa tapaa europarlamentaarikko Maria Guzeninan Euroopan parlamentissa Brysselissä 1. lokakuuta 2026. Maria Guzenina toimii varajäsenenä kulttuuri- ja koulutusvaliokunnan (CULT) komiteassa ainoana pohjoismaisena europarlamentaarikkona. Matkalle osallistuvat Kulttuuri- ja taidealan keskusjärjestö KULTA ry:n jäsenjärjestöjen edustajat.

Ensimmäistä kertaa Euroopan unionin historiassa Euroopan parlamentti, Euroopan unionin neuvosto ja Euroopan komissio sitoutuivat virallisesti yhteiseen poliittiseen tavoitteeseen nostaa kulttuuri EU-politiikan keskiöön allekirjoittamalla julistuksen, ”Eurooppa kulttuurin puolesta ja kulttuuri Euroopan puolesta”, Brysselissä 18. kesäkuuta 2026. 

”Maailman muuttuva toimintaympäristö korostaa eurooppalaisen yhteistyön merkitystä myös kulttuuripolitiikassa. Kulttuuri on keskeinen osa demokratiaa, turvallisuutta ja luovien alojen kasvua, ja Suomen on tärkeää olla aktiivisesti mukana rakentamassa eurooppalaista kulttuuripolitiikkaa”, kommentoi Suomen kulttuuri- ja tiedeinstituuttien pääsihteeri Hanna Lämsä matkaa.

title: Kutsu: Collage - stage of things
content:
Neljä taiteilijaa kutsutaan Viirukseen luomaan esitys yhdessä.
He eivät tunne toisiaan. He tulevat erilaisista taiteellisista taustoista.
Taiteilijat tekevät yhteistyötä, haastavat toisiaan ja vaikuttavat toistensa työhön, yrittäen löytää uusia yhteyksiä tällä kaoottisella aikakaudella.

Yhdellä taiteilijoista on visio hammaslääkärin huoneesta ja sumerilaisesta hammasmadosta, yhtä inspiroi käsite kehoista ilman sisäelimiä sekä praktiikka nimeltä staying with, yksi on kiinnostunut kivun esittämisestä ja kuinka haavat rakentuvat, ja yksi haluaa työskennellä romanttisen aikakauden kanssa edeten kohti näkymätöntä vuorta.

Kompromissien sijaan he päättävät löytää keinoja olla läsnä toistensa taideteoksissa – joka on hauskaa, traagista ja naurettavaa yhtäaikaa.
He kutsuvat työtä eläväksi kollaasiksi. Se on mahdollisesti jonkin uuden ja tuntemattoman alku, uusi aikakausi joka on vielä löytämättä.

Viirukseen kutsutut taiteilijat ovat koreografi Jenni-Elina von Bagh (Suomi), monialainen taiteilija Majula Drammeh (Ruotsi), kuva- ja performanssitaiteilija Nastja Säde Rönkkö (Suomi) ja teatteriohjaaja Gosia Wdowik (Puola).

title: Kolari ja metsänvartija – eli torppari toisin nähtynä
content: Vuonna 1766 Loimaan Joenperässä Vähätalon isäntä Simo Heikinpoika päätti perustaa tilansa maille torpan, koska palvelusväen saanti oli vaikeaa. Onnekseen hän pääsi sopimukseen veljensä Tuomas Heikinpojan kanssa.  Tuomas sai eliniäkseen käyttöönsä sovitut pellot ja niityt sekä kotitaloutensa tarvitsemat rakennukset. Näitä etuja vastaan hän lupasi tehdä veljelleen kaksi päivää työtä joka viikko. Ajatus torpparista tilan työmiehenä on tuttu niin historiantutkimuksesta kuin kaunokirjallisuudestakin. Harvemmin vastaan tulee kuvauksia siitä, mitä muuta torppari vuokranantajalleen saattoi olla. Torpparin erilaisia rooleja pohdiskelin luettuani noin puolitoista tuhatta torpankontrahtia Huittisista, Loimaalta ja Jokioisten kartanosta.

title: Pahamaineinen data-analytiikkayhtiö Palantir valtaa yhä enemmän alaa avustussektorilla – ”Ihmettelemme, miksi tästä ei puhuta enempää”
content:
Vuosi sitten Maailman ruokajärjestö WFP:n sisältä kuului korkean prioriteetin varoitus. Järjestössä oli herännyt huoli, että miljoonien haavoittuvaisessa asemassa olevien ihmisten data ei ollut turvassa.

WFP:n tarkastusviraston raportti vuoti julkisuuteen viime kesänä, ja se nosti esille useita huolenaiheita WFP:n yhteistyössä datateknologiajätti Palantirin kanssa.

Sisäisestä kritiikistä huolimatta YK:n alainen WFP uusi nyt syksyllä mediatietojen mukaan yhteistyösopimuksensa Palantirin kanssa.

Rose Worden ja Tina Mason ovat työskennelleet avustussektorilla vuosia, ja heitä uutinen hirvittää.

Tutkijakaksikko julkaisi kesäkuussa Tech for Bad -aloitteen ja –raportin, johon he kokosivat kaiken saatavilla olevan tiedon yhteistyöstä Palantirin ja WFP:n välillä. Monta kysymystä jäi auki, sillä WFP on ollut varsin nihkeäsanainen yhteistyön luonteesta ja yksityiskohdista.

”Palantirista on ollut paljon kriittistä julkista keskustelua, esimerkiksi sen yhteistyöstä NHS:n kanssa. Tajusimme, että avustussektorilta ei kuulla mitään samanlaista. Ihmettelemme, miksi tästä ei puhuta enempää”, Mason sanoo.

On epäselvää, kuinka tarkkaa dataa WFP:n hyödynsaajista Palantirin tarjoamassa järjestelmässä on.

title: Why Museums Matter for Young People
content:
Teenagers are swapping phone numbers at the end of a museum workshop. A young person who barely left home for three years is pitching their own exhibition to journalists. High school students in Los Angeles are teaching their younger siblings breathing exercises they first learned in front of a Van Gogh. Here is why museums matter for young people, and why they matter now more than ever.

Ask most people who museums are for, and young people tend to appear in only two roles: the primary school group on a trip, or the child in a buggy on a family day out. Somewhere between those early visits and adulthood, many of them drift away. The teenage and young adult years are often the point when museums lose them.

Yet these are exactly the years when young people most need what museums quietly offer. Anxiety, loneliness and uncertainty about the future are shaping a generation, and the places that traditionally support young people, from schools to youth services, are under strain. Many young people spend their days being measured, graded and compared, online and off.

title: Human knowledge at stake: Wikimedia Foundation makes its case at the United Nations General Assembly
content:
New York, 30 September 2026 – During the 81st session of the United Nations General Assembly (UNGA), the Wikimedia Foundation’s CEO, Bernadette Meehan, and Global Advocacy team traveled to New York City to speak with policymakers, philanthropists, and high-level executives about the importance of protecting human knowledge in the age of AI. 

Throughout the week, the team undertook a range of external engagements, including a fireside chat at the UN headquarters with Melissa Fleming, UN Under-Secretary-General for Global Communications; joining Heather Gerken, President of the Ford Foundation and Nobel Laureates Maria Ressa and Muhammad Yunus on the main stage of the Clinton Global Initiative; and speaking with Dr. Rumman Chowdhury at the Devex Impact House. A number of bilateral meetings were also held with a wide range of UN representatives, technology leaders, and academics from around the world. During the week, our message was the same across every conversation: in the age of AI, we must keep humans at the heart of knowledge online.

title: The US Blacklists Alleged Venezuelan Cyber Crime Mastermind
content:
The U.S. Department of the Treasury on Wednesday announced it had placed on a special blacklist Aníbal Alexander Canelón Aguirre— a Venezuelan who appears on the FBI’s "Ten Most Wanted" list—identifying him as a key link in a financial network for the notorious crime group Tren de Aragua. 

Canelón Aguirre is wanted by the Justice Department for allegedly leading a multi-million dollar ATM fraud scheme. Authorities accuse him of masterminding a jackpotting operation involving malware that when installed allows thieves to direct the bank machine to spew out money.

The alleged Venezuelan hacker topped a list of six Venezuelans and three Mexicans whose names were announced Wednesday as having been added to a group of specially designated nationals. It effectively locks them out of the global financial system. Six of the named are co-defendants of Canelón Aguirre in a U.S. prosecution.

The accused hacker has been on the run, lending his tech skills to the likes of a Romanian mafia operating along Mexico's white-sand beaches and became the cyber "engineer" of the infamous Venezuelan Tren de Aragua gang.

title: The Cable that Changed the World: How Instant Global Communication Began in 1858
content:
The word wireless is going the way of computerized and portable, and for much the same reasons. We no longer regard wireless devices that require no physical connections to anything else as marvels, but as something close to necessities. But our age, with its increasingly common assumptions that information just travels through the air, owes its existence to wires — and, in a historical sense, to one set of wires in particular, whose story is told in the Primal Space video above. Woven into a mighty 2,000-mile-long cable, it was laid across the Atlantic Ocean 168 years ago, enabling the first direct communication link between North America and Europe. Not that intercontinental video sharing was just around the corner.

No, the height of communication technology at the time was the telegraph: the Victorian Internet, if you like, to borrow the title of the book by Economist editor Tom Standage that inspired the video. As a technology, telegraphy itself is quite a bit older than the aforementioned transatlantic cable. One possible starting point is 1746, when scientist Jean-Antoine Nollet managed to send a jolt of static electricity all the way down a line of 200 monks.

title: A Girl Nearly Died After Drinking Raw Milk. The State Did Little to Punish the Unlicensed Farmer Who Sold It.
content:
Sitting in a pediatric intensive care unit last year, watching a ventilator keep her 17-month-old daughter alive, Emily Marris scoured the contents of her phone for evidence to give to California health and food safety investigators. 

She had bought raw goat milk from a farm recommended to her in a Facebook group run by her chiropractor. Marris had hoped the milk, unprocessed and natural, would help with her daughter Brooklyn’s constipation. But doctors now suspected the unpasteurized milk, which hadn’t been heated to kill off pathogens, was the source of the toddler’s severe E. coli infection. 

To the regulators who’d reached out to Marris, the case was a top priority. The farm appeared to be defying state law to sell unregulated raw milk to unsuspecting families; soon, another child, a 6-year-old girl who’d drunk milk from the same farm, would wind up in the same San Diego hospital, with the same potentially fatal illness, needing blood transfusions.

• Etusivu

    Voiko tulevaisuustiedosta tehdä muutakin kuin raportin, esityksen tai skenaarion? Kokemuksellinen ennakointi auttaa muuttamaan abstraktit tulevaisuuskuvat koettaviksi tilanteiksi, jotka herättävät ajatuksia, tunteita ja toimintaa. Tässä 5+1 vinkkiä, joilla pääset alkuun. 

    Asiantuntija, Ennakointi ja koulutus

    Tulevaisuudesta puhutaan usein kaavioina, raportteina ja skenaarioina. Ne ovat tarpeellisia, mutta eivät aina riitä. Mitä monimutkaisemmista muutoksista on kyse, sitä vaikeampaa voi olla hahmottaa, miltä niiden vaikutukset tuntuvat arjessa, työssä, päätöksenteossa tai yhteiskunnassa. Miten esimeriksi siirtymä kiertotalouteen tai neuroteknologian kuluttajakäyttö muuttaisi ihmisten arkea?

    Kokemuksellinen ennakointi tarjoaa tähän yhden vastauksen. Sen tavoitteena ei ole ennustaa tulevaisuutta, vaan tehdä mahdollisia tulevaisuuksia koettaviksi: esineinä, tarinoina, peleinä, simulaatioina, tiloina, rooleina, kehollisina harjoituksina tai muina kokemuksina. Kun tulevaisuus tulee lähemmäs, se voi avata uusia kysymyksiä: mitä tämä tarkoittaisi minulle, meille tai niille, joita päätöksemme koskevat?

title: Kouvolan kirjastoleikkaukset osuisivat lapsiin, senioreihin ja vähävaraisiin
content:
Kouvolassa esitetään Haanojan ja Korian lähikirjastojen lakkauttamista. Jos kirjastot suljetaan, matka kirjastoon pitenee kohtuuttomasti.

Muutos vaikeuttaisi erityisesti lasten, senioreiden ja sellaisten ihmisten asiointia, jotka eivät voi kulkea kauemmas omin avuin tai joilla ei ole käytössään autoa.

Haanojan kirjaston lainaus on kasvanut viisi vuotta peräkkäin. Korialla kirjaston käyttö on jatkunut entisellään. Kirjastot ovat siis ahkerassa käytössä samaan aikaan, kun niiden tulevaisuus on vaakalaudalla.

Kirjastojen toimipisteiden lakkautus tai henkilöstön vähentäminen osuisivat suoraan kirjavinkkaukseen, kouluyhteistyöhön, satutuokioihin eli erityisesti lasten ja nuorten lukemista tukevaan toimintaan.

Myös aikuisten lukutaito heikkenee, sillä kirjasto on yksi harvoista tahoista, joka huolehtii myös aikuisten lukemisesta. Kirjastoissa tehtävä työ palvelee ihmisten juurtumista kotiseutuunsa ja tunnetta kuulumisesta yhteisöön.

Lukutaitoon satsaaminen on ensiarvoisen tärkeää niin Kouvolan kuin koko Suomen kannalta.

title: Inside Zuckerberg, Huang’s push for White House AI pact
content:
Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg was the chief architect of the “morally binding” AI accords that emerged from Tuesday’s White House lunch with President Donald Trump, Speaker Mike Johnson and more than a dozen tech executives, according to five people familiar with the private meeting.

Zuckerberg, with the help of Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang, pitched the so-called AI accords to senior White House officials and some of the biggest names in tech during the luncheon, three of the people said. Both Huang as well as Trump administration officials helped shape the pact ahead of the meeting, according to two of the people.

All five people were granted anonymity because they were not authorized to share details of the discussions.

As part of the voluntary agreement, signatories would commit to the importance of enacting safeguards to mitigate potential risks from advanced AI models, but without a clear enforcement mechanism, it is unclear what if any consequences they may face for failing to do so.

title: Almost everyone naturally turns left when walking – and we still have no idea why
content:
This story began, like so many in the history of science, with something we were not looking for.

In 2020, during the COVID-19 pandemic, we were studying a practical question: how do people move around in an enclosed space when you ask them to keep apart from one another? Watching the footage time after time, we noticed something odd: almost every participant walked in loops that turned in the same direction, always anticlockwise. Stranger still, none of them seemed to have noticed they were doing it.

That observation sent us on a five-year quest to work out why humans behave in this way.

The effect itself is easy to describe. Let a crowd roam within a closed space with no particular destination, and it slowly begins to rotate, almost always to the left. Nobody directs that motion. Nobody decides it.

To a physicist, this looks like a textbook instance of “emergent behavior”: a collective pattern that grows out of countless small interactions, either between individuals or between individuals and their surroundings. These were our two prime hypotheses, which we tried to validate in isolation.
snippet: This story began, like so many in the history of science, with something we were not looking for.

title: Cities across the world are sinking because of groundwater depletion. But the process can be reversed
content:
Many cities around the world are sinking because too much water is extracted from the groundwater reservoirs beneath them.

This sinking makes these coastal cities more exposed to rising seas as the climate warms.

But as our new research shows, this process can work in reverse; when groundwater is replenished, cities can rise.

Our findings also reveal an unexpected clue: faultlines play a key role in shaping where the fastest groundwater recovery and land uplift occur.

Land subsidence, the gradual sinking of the ground surface, affects many of the world’s major cities.

Parts of Jakarta, the capital of Indonesia, are sinking more than ten centimetres each year, prompting the government to plan a relocation of the city.

The coastal city of Tianjin, China, is home to 15 million people. It, too, is a subsidence hotspot. If sinking there continues unabated, 15% of the city’s population will be underwater by 2120.

Similar stories are playing out from San Diego to Iran’s major cities, wherever groundwater has been pumped faster than it can refill.
snippet: Many cities around the world are sinking because too much water is extracted from the groundwater reservoirs beneath them.

title: Report: Climate risks could multiply disruptions to Finland’s security of supply
content:
Climate change threatens Finland’s security of supply by increasing the likelihood of simultaneous crises and disruptions. Finland must prepare for climate risks as part of geopolitical crises and security policy, states a new report by the Finnish Institute of International Affairs (FIIA) and the National Emergency Supply Agency (NESA).

“Climate risks cannot be treated as something that we can circle back to once military crises are over,” says Leading Researcher Emma Hakala from FIIA, who headed the research project.

For example, extreme weather events can disrupt production, transport and the supply of critical raw materials, all of which are essential for security of supply, while the very same supply chains are being hindered by wars and trade disputes.

“This year, heatwaves caused significant problems across Europe, and the impacts of such phenomena are also quickly felt in Finland,” Hakala points out.

Davvisámegiella | Anarâškielâ

Sámedikki ođđa dutkanehtalaš ráđđi nanosmahttá sámiid vejolašvuođaid oassálastit sámiid guoski dutkama ehtalaš árvvoštallamii. Ráđi bargun lea ovddidit dutkanehtalaš rávvagiid ollašuvvama, mearridit sámiid searvvušlaš ovdamiehtamiin ja ovddidit ovdamiehtanmeannudeami.

Dutkanehtalaš ráđđi čoahkkanii vuosttas háve 29.9.2026. title: Immo Salonen appointed CEO of Profinder
content:
Immo Salonen has been appointed the new CEO of Profinder, taking up his position at the beginning of November 2026. In his new role, Salonen will also lead Liana, both part of the Ilkka Group.

Salonen joins Profinder from his role as CEO of Auntie Solutions. He has previously held leadership positions at companies including LINK Mobility, TietoEVRY and Giosg.

Salonen’s appointment marks the next phase in Profinder’s development, with a continued focus on growth, data-driven sales and marketing, and expanding the company’s international opportunities.

“Profinder has built a strong position through its expertise in data-driven sales and marketing. I see significant potential to build on this foundation and accelerate growth. Together with Liana, there are also opportunities to combine complementary data, technology and commercial expertise to create new value for customers,” says Immo Salonen.

Profinder and Liana will continue to operate as separate businesses, with their own brands, teams and services. Existing customer agreements and contact persons remain unchanged, and the appointment will not affect customers’ day-to-day business.

title: “East of Eden” Is at the Library; Now It Comes to TV
content:
Florence Pugh and Zoe Kazan, the star and screenwriter (respectively) of Netflix’s “East of Eden,” a fresh take on John Steinbeck’s classic 1952 California novel, recently came to the Library to get a look at some original Steinbeck material.

Among other items on display, there were signed first editions of “Eden,” manuscript pages from “The Grapes of Wrath” and a dozen or so books from the 19th and early 20th centuries that documented the land and the people of the Salinas Valley, the primary setting of “Eden,” “Of Mice and Men” and other Steinbeck works.

The seven-episode series, which debuts tomorrow,  will stretch, like the book, from the end of the Civil War to World War I. It will also be a tale of good and evil, like the book, but is more centered around the lightning rod character of Cathy Ames, played by Pugh.

“I believe there are monsters born in the world to human parents,” Steinbeck writes in introducing Cathy in the novel, a famous sentence that also begins the series’ trailer, already viewed more than 5 million times on YouTube alone.

title: Tutkimus: Ilmastoriskit voivat moninkertaistaa Suomen huoltovarmuushäiriöt
content:
Ilmastonmuutos uhkaa Suomen huoltovarmuutta lisäämällä samanaikaisten kriisien ja häiriötilanteiden todennäköisyyttä. Ilmastoriskeihin on varauduttava osana geopoliittisia kriisejä ja turvallisuuspolitiikkaa, todetaan Ulkopoliittisen instituutin (UPI) ja Huoltovarmuuskeskuksen (HVK) raportissa.

”Ilmastoriskeihin ei voida suhtautua jonakin, johon voidaan palata sitten, kun sotilaalliset kriisit ovat ohi”, sanoo tutkimushanketta vetänyt UPIn johtava tutkija Emma Hakala.

Esimerkiksi äärisäät voivat häiritä huoltovarmuuden kannalta olennaista tuotantoa, kuljetuksia ja kriittisten raaka-aineiden saatavuutta samalla, kun sodat ja kauppakiistat vaikeuttavat samojen toimitusketjujen toimintaa.

”Tänä vuonna helle aiheutti Euroopassa merkittäviä ongelmia, ja vaikutukset heijastuvat nopeasti myös Suomeen”, Hakala huomauttaa.

Samat ongelmat toistuvat eri aloilla

Tutkimuksessa tarkasteltiin ilmastonmuutoksen vaikutuksia lääkehuoltoon, kriittisiin raaka-aineisiin, lannoitteisiin ja sähköistyvään energiajärjestelmään. Kaikilla aloilla toistuivat samat ongelmat. Tuotanto on keskittynyt harvoihin maihin, ja se on riippuvaista yksittäisistä toimittajista.

title: Malaysia begins Myanmar repatriations despite warnings from UN and rights groups
content:
Kuala Lumpur plans to send a total of 5,000 Myanmar nationals back to the war-torn country despite persecution concerns

Malaysia began sending back about 1,500 Myanmar nationals on Tuesday, the government confirmed, as it launched a scheme that rights groups say may endanger migrants and asylum seekers by returning them to the war-torn country.

The group is the first of 5,000 Myanmar citizens that Kuala Lumpur says agreed to “voluntary” repatriation from detention centres amid a huge uptick in anti-migrant sentiment in Malaysia.

title: Avointa tarinaa vaikeista ratkaisuista
content:
Eero Karisto

Riitta ja Ilkka -kirjassa kulkevat rinnakkain Suomisen vanhempien sekä Riikka Suomisen oma rakkaustarina. Kirja ei ole romanttista huttua vaan ihan todellista tilanteiden, prosessien ja tunne-elän kuvausta. Ihmisten pohtimista vaikeiden ratkaisujen äärellä.

On mielenkiintoista lukea kirjaa, johon on henkilökohtainen suhde, autofiktiota ihmisistä, jotka on tuntenut – ja kirjaa, jonka taustakeskusteluihin on kirjoitusprosessin alkuvaiheessa itsekin pienellä vaatimattomalla panoksellaan osallistunut.

Päähenkilöiden lisäksi muitakin tuttuja ihmisiä vilahtelee kirjassa, samoin tapahtumia, joihin on itsekin osallistunut. Ihmisiä Suominen kuvaa oivaltavasti, kertoo anekdootteja, sitaatteja ja ajatuksia, joista löytää oleellisia piirteitä tutuista ihmisistä.

Tiedot vanhempien Suomisten tarinasta perustuvat heidän kirjeenvaihtoonsa sekä keskusteluihin pariskunnan tuttavien kanssa, toki mielikuvitusta unohtamatta.

title: Lawyer Cites ChatGPT-Invented Fake Witnesses in Murder Appeal
content:
A lawyer used ChatGPT to generate briefs that included completely made-up witnesses and testimony while representing a man accused of shooting his wife. When he was caught by the judges, the lawyer blamed it on his own “stupidity.” 

“It's little comfort to know that my stupidity is what brings us together this afternoon,” New Mexico attorney Stephen D. Aarons said in a hearing last month before five judges. He “assumed” ChatGPT would generate a “bulletproof summary of proceedings.” Instead, ChatGPT generated false testimony from “wholly fabricated witnesses,” according to an order of direct contempt from the New Mexico Supreme Court. Aarons was representing a man who was found guilty of killing his wife earlier this year; Aarons said he hadn’t told his client directly that he was caught using ChatGPT on the case because he’s currently serving life in prison.

Less than two weeks after the US revealed a Russian plot to assassinate dissidents in Washington, the FSB turned its crosshairs on London.

title: German innovation award recognises CMI’s pioneering digital approach to peacemaking
content:
The Round Table for Mediation and Conflict Management of the German Economy (RTMKM) has named CMI the winner of its 2026 Innovation Prize for Mediation and Conflict Management at an award ceremony in Frankfurt am Main on 22 September.

CMI – Martti Ahtisaari Peace Foundation has won a prize for innovation in mediation and conflict management for its AI-supported consultation that increased young people’s participation in its work with Yemeni political parties.

Felix Kufus (fourth left) at the prize ceremony. He led CMI’s development and implementation of the approach.

The prize by the Round Table for Mediation and Conflict Management of the German Economy recognises innovative approaches that promote alternative dispute resolution or conflict prevention.

Eligible innovations could be procedural, substantive, technical or non-technical, but had to be theoretically grounded, already applied in practice and respond to a recognisable demand.

“Digital innovation is most valuable when it helps us hear voices that might otherwise go unheard,” said Johanna Poutanen, Head of CMI’s Inclusion and Digital Innovation team.

title: "No Land to Stand On": Mahmoud Khalil on His Memoir, Palestine, Fighting Deportation & Suing Columbia
content:
We speak with Palestinian activist Mahmoud Khalil about his new memoir, No Land to Stand On: Notes from Detention. It details his 104 days of detention inside a Louisiana ICE jail after he was targeted for arrest and deportation by the Trump administration over his pro-Palestine campus advocacy at Columbia University. Khalil missed the birth of his first child, Deen, while he was separated from his wife, Noor Abdalla, who is a U.S. citizen. The administration is still trying to deport Khalil, who has launched civil rights lawsuits against the government and Columbia University over his treatment.

“Eighteen months after my arrest, this administration has never charged me with any crime or even presented any evidence that I committed any crimes, yet they are able to get away with this because I’m Palestinian,” Mahmoud tells Democracy Now!

title: Erkki Tuomioja: Ilmastouhkien torjuntaa ei pidä politiikasta unohtaa
content:
Arviot ilmastonmuutoksen seurauksista eivät enää perustu teoreettisiin skenaarioihin. Näyttöjäkin on: tappavat helteet, tuhoisat maastopalot ja jäätikköromahdukset.

Siksi voikin varauksetta yhtyä Ekosäätiön Pekka Kuusi -palkinnolla äskettäin palkitun Kestävyyspaneelin visioon:

Luonnon ja ihmisten hyvinvointi on asetettava politiikan ensisijaiseksi tavoitteeksi, tehtävä talous reiluksi niin että se toimii luonnon kantokyvyn rajoissa, ja on nostettava planetaarinen turvallisuus päätöksenteon keskiöön.

Jos nämä periaatteet löytyvät seuraavan hallituksen ohjelmasta, on vielä eri asia esitetäänkö myös käytännön toimia niiden toteuttamiseksi ja tullaanko niitä myös täytäntöön panemaan.

TUTKITUN tiedon asema politiikassa on haastettu. Voimistunut pölhöpopulismi vähättelee tieteellistä tutkimusta ja nostaa maallikkomielipiteet sen rinnalle.

Totuuden jälkeisenä aikana saatetaan vuosikymmenten empiirinen tutkimus ja tiedeyhteisön konsensus kuitata vain ”yhtenä
mielipiteenä muiden joukossa”.

Tieteenvastaisuus tuskin estää kestävyyspaneelin tavoitteiden hallitusohjelmaan ottamisen.

title: Fourth Edition of Bangla Wikibooks Writing Contest Concludes Successfully
content:
The fourth edition of the Bangla Wikibooks Writing Contest, “Wikibooks Writing Contest 2026“, closed with 1,440,402 accepted words from its eligible participants, well ahead of both the 2024 and 2025 editions. A total of 2,088 pages were submitted and every one of them was reviewed.

Like the 2025 edition, the contest was organised as part of the “Bangla WikiConnect” initiative. It invited new and experienced volunteers to build free, book-length educational content in the Bangla language on Bangla Wikibooks.

The contest ran from 1 May, 2026 to 3 June, 2026. Submissions were tracked on Fountain, and the final results are published on the results page.

49 participants submitted a total of 2,088 pages. Of these, 46 participants were eligible for ranking, and 37 of them had at least one page accepted.

The eligible participants contributed 1,440,402 accepted words across 1,401 submitted pages. Seven participants each passed 100,000 accepted words, and 15 passed 10,000.

By word count, 81% of what eligible participants submitted was accepted: 1,440,402 of 1,775,897 words.

The first-place winner alone contributed 338,327 accepted words, and the top three together contributed 734,922.

title: Has Russia deployed 80,000 troops near the Latvian and Estonian borders?
content:
Talk of possible mobilisation in Russia, together with reports that the aggressor state is preparing up to 20,000 beds in civilian hospitals near the Baltic Sea, has added to public concern. But public anxiety also creates fertile ground for false information.

In early September, a social media post claimed that Russia had deployed a “new army” of up to 80,000 troops near its borders with Latvia and Estonia, citing purported information from Lithuanian intelligence. The claim is false.

On 1 September this year, an anonymous account called “Кассандра” (Kassandra) published a post on Threads with an alarming introduction: “Don’t make any plans for autumn. We’re taking the Baltics. Lithuanian intelligence reports that the Baltic people are soon going to be ***.” The post claimed that Russian armed forces had moved hundreds of military trucks to the borders with Latvia and Estonia, that new offensive divisions had been formed from brigades stationed there, and that the total strength of this “new army” was between 50,000 and 80,000 troops.

The post also claimed that “fresh satellite images confirm the troop buildup. The concentration of equipment is alarming NATO and the Baltic people.”

title: Who can speak on behalf of the people? The new frontiers of protest in the Sahel
content:
Can a democracy exist without the right to disagree?

Originally published on Global Voices

Demonstrations in the Sahel: (left) Mali, (center) Niger, and (right) Burkina Faso. Screenshots via YouTube.

This post is part of Global Voices’ September 2026 Spotlight series, “Protest in Democracy.” With this Spotlight, we seek to explore the many forms of protest, the tactics states use to delegitimize and suppress them, and the complex relationship between protest and democracy. You can support this coverage by donating here.

In the countries of the central Sahel, Mali, Burkina Faso, and Niger, military juntas present themselves as the voices of restored popular sovereignty. At the same time, political parties have been dissolved in all three countries, more than a thousand civil society organizations have been suspended in Burkina Faso, and labor unions are under attack in Niger. What becomes of the right to protest when those in power claim to embody the very people on whose behalf the protests are being held?

title: Russia Challenges South Africa’s Exclusion From G20 Summit
content:
By Kester Kenn Klomegah*

MOSCOW | NEW YORK | 30 September 2026 (IDN) — At the 81st UN General Assembly in New York, Russian Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov reiterated Russia’s objection to South Africa’s exclusion from the forthcoming G20 summit in the United States, while emphasising the importance of multilateral institutions and the place of Africa in the emerging international order.

Lavrov described in some detail Russia’s assessment of the current state of relations with the United States. His remarks also touched on broader questions confronting Africa and other countries of the Global South and East as they seek to strengthen the multilateral foundations of the international system and counter what they regard as neocolonial practices.

The 2026 G20 Leaders’ Summit is scheduled for Miami, Florida, on 14–15 December. The United States has invited Russian President Vladimir Putin to attend, an invitation US Secretary of State Marco Rubio confirmed after talks with Lavrov on the sidelines of the UN General Assembly.

title: Inbjudan: Collage - stage of things
content:
Fyra konstnärer bjuds in till Viirus för att tillsammans skapa en föreställning.
De känner inte varandra sedan tidigare. De har olika konstnärliga bakgrunder.
Konstnärerna samarbetar, utmanar och påverkar varandra i sökandet efter nya kopplingar i denna kaotiska tid.

En konstnär har en vision om en tandläkarmottagning och den sumeriska tandmasken, en är inspirerad av konceptet kroppar utan organ och arbetsmetoden staying with, en är intresserad av hur man utövar smärta och skapar sår, och en vill arbeta med romantiken och bege sig mot ett osynligt berg.

Istället för att kompromissa bestämmer de sig för att kollidera och hitta sätt att vara närvarande i varandras konstverk – det är roligt, tragiskt och löjligt på samma gång. De kallar det för ett levande kollage. Det är möjligen början på något okänt, en ny era som ännu ska upptäckas.

De inbjudna gästerna är koreografen Jenni-Elina von Bagh (FIN), tvärkonstnären Majula Drammeh (SE), bild- och performancekonstnären Nastja Säde Rönkkö (FIN), och teaterregissören Gosia Wdowik (PL).

Collage – stage of things är ett tvärkonstnärligt verk som utmanar individualism, separation och ägandeskap.

title: From Tagging to Togetherness: How Art UK Turned a Digital Tool into Real-World Connection
content:
A simple artwork-tagging tool has become the starting point for friendships, wellbeing and a renewed pride in place. At the Digital Collections Summit, Art UK’s Katey Goodwin and Natalie Willatt explained how.

Digital collections work is often measured in records, clicks and page views. But what happens when a national online platform is deliberately turned into something local, social and face-to-face?

That was the question behind a talk at the Digital Collections Summit by Katey Goodwin, Deputy Chief Executive and Director of Community Engagement at Art UK, and Natalie Willatt, the organisation’s Community Volunteer Manager. Using Art UK’s community volunteering programme in Stoke-on-Trent as a case study, they showed how a crowdsourcing tool called Tagger has sparked genuine human connection, reduced isolation and strengthened people’s relationship with art and place.

As Goodwin put it, Art UK’s mission is simple: to connect people with art. This programme set out to test whether art could also become a catalyst for connecting people with one another.

title: Čitna Báffa
content:
Čitna Báffa är ett tvärvetenskapligt verk av den samiska bildkonstnären Máret Ánne Sara och koreografen Alexandra Wingate, som förenar bildkonst, koreografi, rörelse och ljud. Verket utforskar en existentiell spänning mellan ett yttre liv som präglas av det västerländska industrisamhället och kapitalismen, och en inre värld som grundar sig på samisk filosofi och urfolkskunskap.

Det konstnärliga utforskandet inleddes med SuoidneKaboom (2023) och utvecklades vidare till föreställningen Čitna Báffa och utställningen Háhtešeatni doali dádjadit. I dessa verk utforskar konstnärerna hur bildkonst och scenkonst samverkar, påverkar och förvandlar varandra, där bildkonstverken existerar både självständigt och i dialog med levande kroppar och rörelse.

Projektet, som har sina rötter i samiska och arktiska sammanhang, samlar konstnärer från hela Norden, lyfter fram samiska perspektiv och skapar möten mellan publik, konstnärer och kulturaktörer. Čitna Báffa och Háhtešeatni doali dádjadit presenterades vid Festspillene i Nord-Norge i Harstad, medan SuoidneKaboom framfördes vid Riddu Riđđu, Suialaa Art Festival, Sámi Dáiddaguovddáš och Sámi Beassášmárkanat.

title: Fiji Overhauls Evidence Security After 52 Kilos of Cocaine Vanish from Court
content:
Fiji’s police chief has ordered the immediate transfer of all illicit drugs and cash to highly secure police vaults after officials confirmed Wednesday that 52.4 kilograms of cocaine tied to two major criminal cases were stolen from a High Court evidence room, in the capital, Suva, with much of the contraband replaced by flour.

The incident is seen as a significant blow to a police force already struggling with corruption allegations amid a surge in international drug trafficking. However, Police Commissioner Rusiate Tudravu maintained that police are not responsible for guarding evidence once it is transferred to the judiciary, comparing the nation’s High Court to a private residence.

“It’s just like your home,” he told an OCCRP reporter. “You’re the boss of your home. I cannot come and tell you I’ll guard your home. Simple.”

Fiji, a nation of fewer than a million people, is facing an escalating drug crisis. It has become a transit hub for cocaine smuggled from South America to Australia and New Zealand, and is now seeing a spike in domestic use driving soaring HIV rates linked to intravenous methamphetamine use.

title: The Oldest Book Printed with Movable Type is Not The Gutenberg Bible: Jikji, a Collection of Korean Buddhist Teachings, Predated It By 78 Years and It’s Now Digitized Online
content:
The history of the printed word is full of bibliographic twists and turns, major historical moments, and the significant printing of books now so obscure no one has read them since their publication. Most of us have only the sketchiest notion of how mass-produced printed books came into being—a few scattered dates and names. But every schoolchild can tell you the first book ever printed, and everyone knows the first words of that book: “In the beginning….”

The first Gutenberg Bible, printed in 1454 by Johannes Gutenberg, introduced the world to movable type, history tells us. It is “universally acknowledged as the most important of all printed books,” writes Margaret Leslie Davis, author of the 2019 book, The Lost Gutenberg: The Astounding Story of One Book’s Five-Hundred-Year Odyssey. In 1900, Mark Twain expressed the sentiment in a letter “commenting on the opening of the Gutenberg Museum,” writes M. Sophia Newman at Lithub. “What the world is to-day,” he declared, “good and bad, it owes to Gutenberg. Everything can be traced to this source.”

title: Ansök om trycknings- och översättningsstöd i oktober
content:
I oktober kan bokutgivare söka om stöd för att trycka fack- och skönlitteratur på svenska, samt stöd för att översätta böcker från finska till svenska.

Delegationen för den svenska litteraturens främjande handlägger statligt stöd för tryckning av svenskspråkig skön- och facklitterära verk som ges ut i Finland, samt stöd för översättning av finskspråkig skön- och facklitteratur till svenska. Delegationen handlägger även tryckningsstöd ur följande fonder inom SLS: Christian och Constance Westermarcks fond och Ingrid, Margit och Henrik Höijers donationsfond I.

Verket ska ges ut i Finland. Stöd kan sökas av förlag, föreningar och organisationer som ger ut litteratur i Finland. Det går också att söka stöd för böcker utgivna av privatpersoner på eget förlag förutsatt att utlåtanden av två oberoende lektörer bifogas ansökan. Stöd kan inte sökas av bokens författare utan endast av utgivaren.

Stödet utbetalas när avtal har undertecknats och fyra (4) exemplar av den färdiga boken har sänts till SLS.

Aktuell ansökningstid är 1–31.10.2026.

OBS! Frågor gällande ansökan besvaras fram till kl. 16 på fredag 30.10. Frågor kan skickas till adressen delegationen@sls.fi.
snippet: I oktober kan bokutgivare söka om stöd för att trycka fack- och skönlitteratur på svenska, samt stöd för att översätta böcker från finska till svenska.

title: EU and Canada to announce sweeping new partnership pact
content:
BRUSSELS — The EU and Canada will use a landmark summit next month to announce an expansive new partnership, ranging from breaking down digital trade barriers to joint support for Ukraine and investing in fighting wildfires.

“The world is rapidly changing with unprecedented geopolitical challenges as well as challenges across trade, energy, technology, climate, and resources,” reads a draft joint statement to be issued by the two sides, circulated to EU ambassadors in preparation for the planned summit that begins on Oct. 29, and obtained by POLITICO.

The EU and Canada have been seeking to shore up their strategic ties as they grapple with the fallout from U.S. President Donald Trump’s trade war. European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen this month proposed inviting Canada to become an associate member of the EU, triggering an immediate threat by Trump to impose tariffs.

“Canada and the EU, with our unparalleled trade access, shared values, and complementary economic strengths, can build a deeper and more integrated relationship,” the draft paper says.

title: Senate Democrats block datacenter energy bill, saying ‘toothless’ legislation ‘misses the mark’
content:
Republicans supported legislation although Democrats said it wouldn’t effectively address energy consumption

Senate Democrats on Wednesday blocked legislation intended to offset the impact of datacenters on consumer electricity bills, calling it a “toothless” attempt to address a top voter concern ahead of November’s midterm elections.

The Ratepayer Protection Act failed by a 57-to-43 vote, falling just shy of the 60 votes necessary to advance through the Republican-controlled chamber. Four Democrats – Maggie Hassan of New Hampshire, Amy Klobuchar of Minnesota and both Georgia senators, Jon Ossoff and Raphael Warnock – joined Republicans in support of the measure.

title: After a decade, the UN’s Antonio Guterres is stepping down. His legacy will be mixed, at best
content:
In his farewell address to the United Nations General Assembly last week, António Guterres reminisced about his time as secretary general.

In his words, it was a decade during which wars:

dragged on with despicable cruelty. Civilians were targeted. Human rights trampled. Hunger weaponised. Humanitarians killed. International law cast aside.

dragged on with despicable cruelty. Civilians were targeted. Human rights trampled. Hunger weaponised. Humanitarians killed. International law cast aside.

It’s true Guterres and the UN faced increasingly difficult challenges during his decade-long period in office, but as he prepares to depart office at the end of the year, how should his tenure be judged?

There are currently 65 active armed conflicts in the world, the most since 1946.

Two permanent members of the UN Security Council, Russia and the United States, have started wars in violation of the UN Charter.

Meanwhile, tech experts are now warning that AI might wipe out humanity. Accelerating climate change also poses an existential threat.

No UN secretary general could solve all these crises. But historical comparisons are not in Guterres’ favour.

title: Immo Salonen appointed CEO of Liana
content:
Immo Salonen has been appointed the new CEO of Liana, taking up his position at the beginning of November 2026. In his new role, Salonen will also lead Profinder, both part of the Ilkka Group.

Salonen joins Liana from his role as CEO of Auntie Solutions. He has previously held leadership positions at companies including LINK Mobility, TietoEVRY and Giosg.

With Salonen’s appointment, Liana enters its next phase of growth with a continued focus on developing its marketing and communications technology offering, strengthening its international business and creating greater value for customers.

“Liana has a strong position in the market, with established customer relationships, talented people and a strong technology offering. I see significant potential to build on these strengths and accelerate international growth. At the same time, closer cooperation with Profinder creates opportunities to combine complementary expertise in technology, data and marketing,” says Immo Salonen.

title: New regulator of metabolism in response to prolonged fasting identified
content:
The functions of our cells are dependent on the availability of nutrients, that are obtained from the food we eat. If an animal is deprived of food, its whole-body metabolism changes, and cellular functions are maintained first by the use of stored energy and reduction of energy consuming functions, and ultimately by breakdown of tissues to survive upon prolonged starvation. Upon deprivation of food, metabolic reprogramming needs to be coordinated systemically between tissues. Certain organs, such as the liver, function as metabolic hubs that coordinate the systemic response to nutrient deprivation, but how this is achieved on the molecular level is not yet fully understood.

The research group led by   at the University of Helsinki , , and the , has found how cells differentiate between acute and prolonged fasting, which have a very different impact on animal physiology and health.

title: Maahanmuuttajataustaiset lapset: Rasismia on kaikkialla – aikuisten pitäisi puuttua enemmän
content:
Maahanmuuttajataustaiset lapset toivovat päättäjiltä ja aikuisilta nykyistä voimakkaampaa puuttumista rasismiin, syrjintään ja kiusaamiseen.

Lapsiasiavaltuutetun toimisto kokosi keväällä 5.–6.-luokkalaisista maahanmuuttajataustaisista lapsista Nuoret neuvonantajat -tiimin. Yhdentoista lapsen ryhmä kokoontui neljä kertaa keskustelemaan siitä, miten maahanmuuttajataustaisten lasten oikeudet voisivat toteutua Suomessa nykyistä paremmin.

Lasten mukaan hyvän arjen perusta on varsin tavallinen: kaverit, läheiset ihmiset, koulu ja harrastukset. Olennaista on tunne siitä, että kuuluu joukkoon ja että tulee kohdelluksi samalla tavalla kuin muut.

Yksi ryhmään osallistuneista lapsista kuvasi hyvää tilannetta näin:

"Sitä ei nolota oma kansallisuus ja ei kohtaa rasismia, ei koe kiusaamista, ei katsota eri tavalla, häntä kohdellaan samalla tavalla, häntä ei syrjitä, saa kavereita, tuntuu turvalliselta, saa tukea muilta, ja häntä kunnioitetaan."

Lasten mukaan tavallista ja turvallista arkea vaikeuttavat erityisesti kiusaaminen, syrjintä ja rasismi.

Rasismi koettiin laajaksi ja konkreettiseksi ongelmaksi. Se liittyi lasten kokemuksissa usein ihmisen taustaan, kieleen tai ulkonäköön.

title: USPS To Put Cameras in Trucks That Scan Roads for ‘Community Safety’
content:
The United States Postal Service is running a pilot program to put cameras in its mail carrier trucks that continuously scan roads and signs, map roadways and sidewalks, and improve “community safety,” according to a letter posted by a labor union and a statement from the agency to 404 Media. The idea is that, since the trucks are constantly traveling anyway, they can be used as a way to collect data, eventually potentially across the nation.

“The purpose of this pilot is to leverage the Postal Service’s unique ability to collect this valuable data due to the scale and frequency with which our fleet of postal vehicles travel the streets of every community across the country,” the letter, posted by NALC Branch 238 to Facebook, reads.

The letter, written by the United States Postal Service (USPS) Labor Relations to Brian Renfroe, the president of the National Association of Letter Carriers, says the USPS will partner with Next Base, a dashcam company, for the pilot. At the moment, the cameras will be used in the Washington, DC area, and will be installed on a hundred vehicles, the letter says.

title: NATO Drones: Swarm or Be Swarmed
content:
Picture a Ukrainian command center: screens show drones moving into a contested battlespace. Their pictures are relayed back to military operators, but they are also acting in concert through linked communications. Software helps determine which drone is best positioned to continue the mission based on its location, payload, and chances of survival.

The operator assesses the information collected by the drone flight, confirms the target, and makes the final decision on whether to engage. Artificial intelligence accelerates the process, but the human remains in control of the critical decision.

This is what coordinated autonomy means in practice. It does not remove people from warfare. It allows one operator to supervise multiple systems that can navigate, exchange information, and divide tasks even when satellite systems like GPS are jammed, or communications are disrupted. Without this, every drone must be managed separately, decisions take longer, and military units cannot operate at the speed and scale that modern warfare requires.

title: Ruotsin totuuskomissio: Pyytäkää saamelaisilta anteeksi ja hyvittäkää loukkaukset
content:
Ruotsin valtion tulee pikimmiten pyytää anteeksi saamelaisilta, jotka nuoruudessaan pakotettiin koulukoteihin ja työlaitoksiin, vaati maan saamelaisten asemaa tutkinut totuuskomissio keskiviikkona julkaistussa raportissaan.

Lisäksi saamelaisten edut pitää ottaa erityisen tarkasti huomioon, kun tehdään päätöksiä kaivostoiminnasta tai tuulivoimasta, neljän vuoden ajan työskennellyt komissio esittää loppuraportissaan.

Yli tuhatsivuisessa raportissa tutkitaan, miten Ruotsin valtio ja kirkko ovat 400 vuoden ajan kohdelleet saamelaisia ja millaisia seuraamuksia toimilla on ollut.

TOTUUSKOMISSIO on tehnyt yli 70 ehdotusta toimista joihin hallituksen, viranomaisten, museoiden ja kirkon tulisi ryhtyä hyvittääkseen saamelaisten kokemia vääryyksiä.

- Toivon, että tämä johtaa muutokseen ja mahdollisesti myös sovintoon. Ensimmäinen asia, joka valtion pitää tehdä, on tunnustaa ne loukkaukset, jotka tapahtuivat pakkosiirtojen, maiden takavarikointien ja menetysten sekä kielellisten ja kulttuuristen menetysten muodossa, sanoi komissiota johtanut Lena Nyberg uutistoimisto TT:lle.

Ruotsin luterilainen kirkko pyysi jo vuonna 2021 anteeksi saamelaisten kokemia ihmisarvon loukkauksia.

title: The Thanks that drove a Wikimedian
content:
In March 2019, a teenager in Bayombong logged into an old Wikipedia account he’d made when he was nine, undid a piece of vandalism on an article he’d been reading, and closed the tab. Some time after that, a notification arrived: someone he’d never met had thanked him for that edit.

He didn’t chase more of them. He didn’t set out to become a Wikimedian. But that small pop-up, a single click by a stranger on the other side of the world, sat with him.

“I felt appreciated,” Chlod Alejandro told me last week. “I didn’t expect that people would just randomly see it and give you thanks. It felt like I wasn’t as lonely doing wiki work. There was actually somebody there.”

Seven years later, Chlod stood on stage in Paris at Wikimania 2026 as the first-ever recipient of the Community Connector award, a new category in the Wikimedian of the Year honours, and the first Filipino to be recognised in the WOTY awards at all. The through-line between those two moments is a story about what a small piece of interface can carry.

title: The Bank of Latvia has not “printed” new money since 2014. Was Prime Minister Kulbergs wrong?
content:
In the discussion, it was pointed out that “price increases are the direct responsibility of The Bank of Latvia (Latvijas Banka, LB)”. When it was suggested that it “continually “prints” new money”, Prime Minister Andris Kulbergs (United List) replied that the central bank “has not printed money since we joined the eurozone in 2014”. The discussion was joined not only by other users but also by LB, which pointed out that it both “issues euro banknotes and coins and participates in their printing”.

LB’s post on X about money issuance and its involvement in “printing”, as well as the charts it provided, sparked a new thread, with the bank being accused of lying. “Here, the Bank of Latvia is lying. The causes of current inflation are not only the situation in the Middle East or what is happening in Russia, but also monetary policy, specifically the ECB’s interest-rate increases, as well as government policy, spending more than it earns and borrowing even more.”

title: January 2026 Protests: Ali Hemmati and Majid Nikandish Executed
content:
According to HRANA, citing Mizan, the death sentences of Ali Hemmati Sistani and Majid Nikandish were carried out early this morning, September 30, 2026.

The two citizens were arrested during the January 2026 protests in Mashhad. The judiciary has alleged that they were activists and participants on the ground during the protests and were involved in incidents on January 8 in the Tabarsi area of Mashhad that resulted in the deaths of four security personnel.

According to the report, security and law enforcement forces arrested a number of citizens during and after the protests, while others were detained following reviews of footage from city surveillance cameras. Ali Hemmati and Majid Nikandish were among those arrested in this connection, and their cases were referred to judicial authorities.

In its report, Mizan, citing what it described as the “defendants’ confessions,” alleged that during interrogation and judicial proceedings, Ali Hemmati confessed to setting fire to a store, blocking a roadway, and injuring a member of the security forces.

title: What Will the Future Remember? Why Museums Must Start Collecting Social Media Now
content:
Try to imagine studying the Renaissance without its art. Now imagine a historian in 2126 trying to understand our era without hashtags, viral videos or online activism. At the Digital Collections Summit, Craig Middleton (State Library of South Australia) and Caroline Wilson-Barnao (University of Queensland) argued that museums can no longer afford to leave social media out of their collections, and offered a practical roadmap for getting started.

Here’s a thought experiment worth sitting with. A historian 100 years from now wants to understand what it was like to be alive in 2026. What should they be able to see?

Our buildings, newspapers, government records and photographs, certainly. But what about the TikToks, Instagram posts, Facebook groups, memes, WhatsApp conversations and YouTube videos through which so much of contemporary life is actually lived?

For Middleton and Wilson-Barnao, co-authors of Collecting Social Media in Museums (Routledge, 2025), the answer is an obvious yes. The more interesting question is why so many museums are still hesitant to act on it.

title: Egyptian Security Services Arrest Entire Newsroom within 24 Hours
content:
Egyptian security services have arrested six journalists between Monday and Tuesday, all working for local independent investigative journalism platform Matsadaash. According to a statement published by the news platform on Wednesday, the crackdown began with raids on the homes of two of the journalists on Monday evening and early Tuesday morning. Over the following hours, authorities raided the homes of the other journalists working for the platform, without providing “any clear explanation for this escalation or its legal basis,” the statement said.

“With these latest arrests, the entire editorial team in the Matsadaash newsroom is now in detention.”  

In a separate statement, the journalists’ legal representative, the Egyptian Initiative for Personal Rights, said that all six journalists' whereabouts remain unknown, adding that they have not been allowed to contact their families or legal team.

title: EU accused of hiding environmental impact of data centers
content:
The European Union has shielded data centers from public scrutiny about how much energy they use, according to a formal complaint filed Monday against the European Commission.

The complaint lodged this week by Lighthouse Reports, and first reported by POLITICO, accuses the EU executive of setting up rules keeping the public from seeing how much energy and water are used by individual data centers.

This comes as public opposition to power-hungry AI data centers grows across Europe, while energy prices rise.

Lighthouse Reports, a Netherlands-based non-profit conducting cross-border investigations of alleged government and corporate wrongdoing, accuses the Commission of building a “wall of silence” about energy consumption.

EU policymakers are determined “to deny or deter access to, and obfuscate understanding of, how data centers are performing,” reads the complaint filed under the Aarhus Convention, a legally binding international treaty that gives the public rights to information and participation in environmental decision-making.
snippet: The European Union has shielded data centers from public scrutiny about how much energy they use, according to a formal complaint filed Monday against the European Commission.

title: Mitä lumi merkitsee elolliselle luonnolle? – Biologi Arto Marjakankaan tietoteos talvesta ilmestyy
content:

”Halusin koota Suomen oloissa ensimmäisen kokonaisesityksen lumen merkityksestä elolliselle luonnolle. Lumipeite ylläpitää luonnon monimuotoisuutta, mutta nyt lumeen sopeutuneita eliöitä uhkaa talvien lämpeneminen”, Arto Marjakangas kertoo.

Lumipeite ylläpitää luonnon monimuotoisuutta. Lumesta onkin enemmän hyötyä kuin haittaa pohjoisille eliöille, jotka ovat sopeutuneet vuodenaikojen vaihteluun. Marjakangas kertoo, kuinka elämä kietoutuu lumen ympärille talvella ja millä keinoin se muovaa luontoa.

Kirja on kokonaisesitys luonnon talvisesta elämästä Suomen lumisissa ympäristöissä. Se myös kuvaa talvien muuttumista ja sitä, miten talvien lämpeneminen ja lumiolojen muutokset vaikuttavat eliöihin.

The Sustainable Gastronomy course will be held from 27 October to 23 November 2026. The course is led by Senior Researcher Silvia Gaiani of the Ruralia Institute at the University of Helsinki.

Teaching consists of four 1.5-hour live online lectures, a closing panel and eight 45-minute recorded sessions. The course examines the entire food system from a Nordic perspective and covers topics such as food cultures, natural resource management, innovation, sustainable restaurant operations, menu development and storytelling.

Speakers include international names such as British Anthony Bennett, CEO of , who has worked in sustainability, philanthropy and culture. The course also features postdoctoral researcher Maryam Razaei, who has over 15 years of experience in sustainable food systems and represents the research institute and think tank. Mika Kauppinen from will also be lecturing.

The closing panel on 23 November 2026 brings together four experts to discuss the future of gastronomy: Danish food historian Asmus Gamdrup Jensen of ; Chiara Facciotto and Laura Forsman of the University of Helsinki’s , which develops sustainable food systems; and Finnish entrepreneur and investor Jan Ameri.
